Recipe:
Ranger Cookies about 3 dozen From the Kitchen of Orrilla VanOrman Ransom’s Mom
§ion;
This recipe originally came from forest rangers in Colorado, where Ransom's mom was young. It was made in Ransom's home since before he can remember.
Shortening1 Cup Sugar1 Cup Brown Sugar1 Cup Eggs2 Vanilla1 teaspoon Flour2 Cups Baking Soda1 teaspoon Baking Powder½ teaspoon Salt½ teaspoon Oats2 Cups Chocolate Chips1 Cup
Preheat oven to 350°.
Combine Shortening, Sugar and Brown Sugar, then mix well.
Add Eggs and Vanilla, then mix well.
Add Flour, Baking Soda, Baking Powder and Salt, then mix well.
Fold in Oats.
Fold in Chocolate Chips.
Put 1½-inch balls of dough (A little smaller than a golf ball.) on a cookie sheet, ≈3 inches apart.
Bake at 350° for 10-12 minutes.
After cooling, they should still be a little soft. If they are crunchy, they are over-cooked.
After they are cool, they can be stored in Ziploc bags to keep them soft.
The dough can be stored in the fridge for several days before cooking if desired.
If you are somewhere where you have difficulty finding Brown Sugar (which missionaries frequently have to deal with) substitute 1 Cup Sugar and 1 Tablespoon Molasses or Dark Corn Syrup. (See Cooking Basics: Conversions and Substitutions page.)
